description:
Advances: specled.spec_review

Follow-up from critical-review F1 (Medium, test gap) on specled_-3q1 (merged as 0.3.3, PR #8). The must requirement specled.spec_review.gh_pages_privilege_separation is backed only by a workflow_file verification, which in SpecLedEx asserts only that the target file exists and contains the cover-id string (lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex: existence check ~L706, String.contains? cover-id ~L779). It asserts nothing about the YAML job structure, so mix spec.check stays green even if a future edit re-merges the render/deploy jobs, promotes top-level permissions to write, or drops the deploy ref pin. The invariant holds today; only its guard is weak. Proposed fix: add a command-tier verification that parses priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex and asserts the two-job split (render has no write scope; deploy holds the write scopes, needs render, runs no PR code; top-level permissions read-only).

comments.text:
ADMISSION VERIFICATION (specled_-k6s, 2026-07-27)
Cold fresh-context verifier run against the epic base tree (feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors @ e81f9f98).

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: small
Mandate confirmed still applicable as written; no narrowing needed.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
All of it. Two edits:

(A) New test file — suggested path test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs (async: true). Read priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex and parse it with `YamlElixir.read_from_string!/1` (yaml_elixir ~> 2.11 is an unconditional dep, mix.exs:133). The template contains ZERO EEx tags (`grep -c "<%"` = 0), so it parses as plain YAML with no rendering step. Assert the four clauses of the must statement at .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md:221-232:
  1. top-level read-only default: `workflow["permissions"] == %{"contents" => "read"}` — no key whose value is "write".
  2. two-job split: `Map.keys(workflow["jobs"]) |> Enum.sort() == ["deploy", "render"]` and `deploy["needs"]` includes "render".
  3. render holds no write scope: every value in `render["permissions"]` is in ~w(read none) — specifically refute `"pull-requests" => "write"` and `"contents" => "write"`.
  4. deploy holds the write scopes AND runs no PR code: `deploy["permissions"] == %{"contents" => "write", "pull-requests" => "write"}`; every `actions/checkout` step in deploy pins `with.ref` to a base-ref expression (assert it equals "${{ github.base_ref }}", i.e. refute an unpinned checkout and refute any `github.event.pull_request.head` ref); and no deploy step's `run` invokes `mix ` (the PR-code execution surface) — assert `mix ` appears only in render steps.
Falsify each assertion before committing (mutate the template in a scratch copy: merge the jobs, promote top-level permissions to write, drop `needs`, drop the deploy `ref` pin) and confirm the test goes RED for each.
Gotcha for the implementer: yaml_elixir/yamerl is YAML 1.1, so the `on:` key parses as the boolean `true`, not the string "on" (confirmed: top-level keys come back as ['name', True, 'permissions', 'concurrency', 'jobs']). Do not key off `"on"`; if trigger assertions are wanted, look up `true`.

(B) Spec edit — .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md, `spec-verification` block. Append (or insert alongside the other `kind: command` entries, :831-908):
```
- kind: command
  target: mix test test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs
  execute: true
  covers:
    - specled.spec_review.gh_pages_privilege_separation
```
Keep the existing `workflow_file` entry at :958-963 as-is — it still carries `specled.spec_review.gh_pages_distribution`, which has no other backing.

Optional, not required by any gate (checked: no "must requirement without scenario" detector exists in lib/): a `spec-scenarios` block covering the id.

== EXPECTED TOUCHES ==
test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs, .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md

== RISK NOTES ==
- Realization-hash gate: NO impact. .spec/realization_hashes.json has exactly one top-level subject key, "api_boundary" (`json.load(...).keys() == ['api_boundary']`); `grep -n "spec_review" .spec/realization_hashes.json` returns nothing. A new test file plus a spec verification entry adds no public API and touches no realized_by binding, so no baseline regeneration is needed.
- Conflict with specled_-ako: it is the only other ticket in the set advancing specled.spec_review. Its stated fix targets lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex and test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs, not the spec file — but if it also repoints/edits the `spec-verification` block of .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md, both tickets write the same block (:831-965). Land them in either order but expect a textual merge in that block; the two edits are semantically independent (different requirement ids, different verification entries).
- Doc-lint corpus counts (specled_-4pl, specled_-yds, specled_-ozm advance specled.package): the new spec verification lines introduce no `verification_`, `requirement_`, `decision_`, or `detector_` stem occurrences, and test/**/ is out of scope for test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs (which is scoped to docs/skills/.spec). Low but nonzero interaction if 4pl re-derives absolute spec-corpus counts after this lands — 4pl should recount AFTER vbo, not before.
- `execute: true` means bare `mix spec.check` will run the new test on every preflight. Keep it pure File.read + YAML parse (no shelling out, no mix task invocation) so it stays sub-second.
- No ordering dependency on any other ticket in the set. The requirement text at .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md:221-232 is not touched by any other ticket in the set.
- Do not weaken the requirement to fit a cheap test: the mandate is a command-tier guard, so a `workflow_file`-with-more-substrings shortcut does not satisfy it.

SCOPE CONTRACT (orchestrator, specled_-k6s — 2026-07-27)

Authoritative for mechanical scope checks. Supplements, does not replace, the
ADMISSION VERIFICATION comment's mandate (items A and B), which is what you implement.

## Allowed touches
- `test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs` (new, `async: true`)
- `.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md` — the `spec-verification` block ONLY. Append
  the new `kind: command` entry. Spec co-change is AUTHORIZED and is the point of
  item B.

## Out of Scope (files)
- `priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex` — you READ it and you will
  temporarily mutate a SCRATCH COPY to prove each assertion red. The committed
  diff must not contain it. The workflow itself is correct; this ticket adds the
  guard, not a fix.
- `mix.exs` / `mix.lock` — `yaml_elixir ~> 2.11` is already an unconditional dep.
  Adding a dependency is a scope violation.
- The `workflow_file` verification entry at ~:958-963 — leave it as-is. It still
  carries `specled.spec_review.gh_pages_distribution`, which has no other backing.
- The requirement text at ~:221-232 — it is correct. Do not edit it.
- `lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex`, `test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs` —
  specled_-ako owns those.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (orchestrator consolidates once at the end), `VERSION`,
  `.spec/realization_hashes.json`, `.spec/state.json`.
- Every file not listed under Allowed touches.

## Out of Scope (intent)
- Do NOT weaken the requirement to fit a cheap test. The mandate is a
  COMMAND-tier guard. A `workflow_file`-with-more-substrings shortcut does not
  satisfy it and will be bounced.
- The new test is `execute: true`, so bare `mix spec.check` runs it on every
  preflight. Keep it pure `File.read` + YAML parse. No shelling out, no mix task
  invocation, sub-second.
- YAML 1.1 gotcha: `on:` parses as the boolean `true`, not the string `"on"`.
  Do not key off `"on"`.
- No `spec-scenarios` block is required by any gate; adding one is optional.

## FALSIFIABILITY BAR — required before commit
Prove each of the four clauses RED against a mutated scratch copy of the
template: merge the two jobs; promote top-level `permissions` to write; drop
`needs`; drop the deploy `checkout` `ref` pin. Confirm the corresponding
assertion fails for each. Paste the four red outputs into your completion record
and record the mutations in the COMMIT MESSAGE. A privilege-separation guard
that was never seen to fail is worthless.

## Verification (change-scoped, run-until-green; host mix, no compose)
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs`
3. `mix format --check-formatted`
4. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`

Do NOT run bare `mix spec.check` and do NOT run the full suite. The orchestrator
owns whole-system proof at the merge gate and PR CI.

title: Command-tier verification for spec_review privilege-split (workflow_file only checks file presence)
